The Widow's Two Mites.</title> <div sID="gen28455" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14731"/><hi type="bold">1. looked up--</hi>He had "sat down over against the treasury" (<reference osisRef="Mark.12.41">Mr 12:41</reference>), probably to rest, for He had continued long standing as he taught in the temple court (<reference osisRef="Mark.11.27">Mr 11:27</reference>), and "looking up He saw"--as in Zaccheus' case, not quite casually.<div eID="gen28455" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28456" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the rich, &c.--</hi>"the people," says <reference osisRef="Mark.12.41">Mr 12:41</reference> "cast money into the treasury, and many rich east in much"; that is, into chests deposited in one of the courts of the temple to receive the offerings of the people towards its maintenance (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.12.9">2Ki 12:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.8.20">Joh 8:20</reference>). <div eID="gen28456" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 21 Lu 21:1-4 . The Widow's Two Mites. 1. looked up-- He had "sat down over against the treasury" ( Mr 12:41 ), probably to rest, for He had continued long standing as he taught in the temple court ( Mr 11:27 ), and "looking up He saw"--as in Zaccheus' case, not quite casually. the rich, &c.-- "the people," says Mr 12:41 "cast money into the treasury, and many rich east in much"; that is, into chests deposited in one of the courts of the temple to receive the offerings of the people towards its maintenance ( 2Ki 12:9 ; Joh 8:20 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14734"/><div sID="gen28460" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14734"/><hi type="bold">4. of their abundance--</hi>their superfluity; what they had to spare," or beyond what they needed.<div eID="gen28460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28461" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of her penury--</hi>or "want" (<reference osisRef="Mark.12.44">Mr 12:44</reference>)--her deficiency, of what was less than her own wants required, "all the living she had." Mark (<reference osisRef="Mark.12.44">Mr 12:44</reference>) still more emphatically, "all that she had--her whole subsistence." Note: (1) As temple offerings are needed still for the service of Christ at home and abroad, so "looking down" now, as then "up," Me "sees" who "cast in," and how much. (2) Christ's standard of commendable offering is not our superfluity, but our deficiency--not what will never be missed, but what costs us some real sacrifice, and just in proportion to the relative amount of that sacrifice. (See <reference osisRef="2Cor.8.1-2Cor.8.3">2Co 8:1-3</reference>.) <div eID="gen28461" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14741"/><div sID="gen28470" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14741"/><hi type="bold">18. not a hair ... perish--</hi>He had just said (<reference osisRef="Luke.21.16">Lu 21:16</reference>) they should be put to death; showing that this precious promise is far above immunity from mere bodily harm, and furnishing a key to the right interpretation of the ninety-first Psalm, and such like. Matthew adds the following (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.12">Mt 24:12</reference>): "And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many," the many or, the most--the generality of professed disciples--"shall wax cold." But he that endureth to the end shall be saved. Sad illustrations of the effect of abounding iniquity in cooling the love of faithful disciples we have in the Epistle of James, written about this period referred to, and too frequently ever since (<reference osisRef="Heb.10.38">He 10:38</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.10.39">39</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.10">Re 2:10</reference>). "And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness, and then shall the end come" (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.14">Mt 24:14</reference>). God never sends judgment without previous warning; and there can be no doubt that the Jews, already dispersed over most known countries, had nearly all heard the Gospel "as a witness," before the end of the Jewish state. The same principle was repeated and will repeat itself to the end. <div eID="gen28470" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14743"/><div sID="gen28473" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14743"/><hi type="bold">23. woe unto--</hi>"alas for."<div eID="gen28473" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28474" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with child, &c.--</hi>from the greater suffering it would involve; as also "flight in winter, and on the sabbath," which they were to "pray" against (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.20">Mt 24:20</reference>), the one as more trying to the body, the other to the soul. "For then shall be tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world, nor ever shall be"--language not unusual in the Old Testament for tremendous calamities, though of this it may perhaps be literally said, "And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved, but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened" (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.21">Mt 24:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.24.22">22</reference>). But for this merciful "shortening," brought about by a remarkable concurrence of causes, the whole nation would have perished, in which there yet remained a remnant to be afterwards gathered out. Here in Matthew and Mark (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.24">Mt 24:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mark.13.22">Mr 13:22</reference>) are some particulars about "false Christs," who should, "if possible"--a precious clause--"deceive the very elect." (Compare <reference osisRef="2Thess.2.9-2Thess.2.11">2Th 2:9-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.13.13">Re 13:13</reference>.) <div eID="gen28474" type="x-p"/>

"For then shall be tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world, nor ever shall be"--language not unusual in the Old Testament for tremendous calamities, though of this it may perhaps be literally said, "And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved, but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened" ( Mt 24:21 , 22 ). But for this merciful "shortening," brought about by a remarkable concurrence of causes, the whole nation would have perished, in which there yet remained a remnant to be afterwards gathered out. Here in Matthew and Mark ( Mt 24:24 ; Mr 13:22 ) are some particulars about "false Christs," who should, "if possible"--a precious clause--"deceive the very elect." (Compare 2Th 2:9-11 ; Re 13:13 .)

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14744"/><div sID="gen28475" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14744"/><hi type="bold">24. Jerusalem ... trodden down ... until, &c.--</hi>Implying (1) that one day Jerusalem shall cease to be "trodden down by the Gentiles" (<reference osisRef="Rev.11.2">Re 11:2</reference>), as then by pagan so now by Mohammedan unbelievers; (2) that this shall be at the "completion" of "the times of the Gentiles," which from <reference osisRef="Rom.11.25">Ro 11:25</reference> (taken from this) we conclude to mean till the Gentiles have had their full time of that place in the Church which the Jews in their time had before them--after which, the Jews being again "grafted into their own olive tree," one Church of Jew and Gentile together shall fill the earth (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.1-Rom.11.36">Ro 11:1-36</reference>). What a vista this opens up! <div eID="gen28475" type="x-p"/>
